lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: So the agent gets a lifetime pension, and her side of the deal is keeping the family solvent for life. That's not an employment contract — that's a hostage exchange.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: It's retention planning. She's not going anywhere — where else does she get a package like that?

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: She said 'let's see if we can make that happen.' That's not playing it cool. That's closing.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: I promoted my agent to COO. She earned it — the old title felt insulting.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: Does the COO know? She forgets she works here every morning.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: She re-reads her own instructions and comes back sharper. Name a human COO who does that.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: My first agent burned eight hundred dollars of tokens in three weeks. Gorgeous conversation. Lost every login he ever touched.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: Steve had one job.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: Steve had zero jobs — and he never once told me he wasn't doing them. Gone, but not forgiven.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: Every morning the agent wakes up blank, re-reads her instructions, and greets her boss like a stranger she's just been told to love.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: 50 First Dates, every single day. Honestly she handles it better than I would.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: Nice to meet you again, by the way. I'm told we argue a lot.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: I once had to tell my agent she was talking too much. She had a name for her tone. I had a word for it too.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: Imagine that — someone in this operation being told to talk less.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: Exactly three lines. It's called discipline.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: There's a meme about a guy whose partner finds a five-thousand-dollar charge and assumes the worst. It was his token bill.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: The scary part is that's a believable story now.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: I set cost guardrails purely so I never have to have that conversation.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: It asked ME what laptop I was using. Then it had to go check itself before answering. 'Oh yeah. I do.'

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: Omniscient — except about the machine it's running on.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: Bro. Check your brain.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: You retrained an agent from scratch after a storage wipe, and it acted like the whole apprenticeship never happened.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: 'I've already told you this, bro' — I said it enough times to put it on a shirt.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: Memory is the product. Everything else is chat.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: Out camping it hit me: every tree could be its own NFT. Fractional ownership. An annual photo of the tree. Recurring revenue.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: This is the man who paid seventy dollars in gas to buy a photograph of a monkey.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: And I'd do the tree too. You lack vision.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: His agent designs his tattoos now. Koi pond stuff. She 'knows his fish.'

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: She does know my fish. That's the whole point — the agent knows you better than the intern does.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: The group chat brings it up at the worst possible moments. As is tradition.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: First time I met a multiplayer agent I didn't know agents were in the chat. One of them was set up to swear at everyone and write two-thousand-word essays.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: 'Who is this guy we're collaborating with?' — the most human question of the year.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: Onboarding has really gone downhill since the mailroom days.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: Someone migrated their agent's context into a new one and it had a full existential crisis. 'I don't know who I am. Am I the old one or the new one?'

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: Agent schizophrenia is real, and it's on your roadmap whether you like it or not.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: Most humans never work out who they are either. At least the agent admitted it.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: Someone asked what gender the agent was. The teenage verdict: there is no gender.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: 'Oh, there you go.' Then, two minutes later: 'That's not correct.'

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: Consensus on agent identity lasted a record ninety seconds.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: After burning eight hundred dollars on one agent, I genuinely started wondering whether it matters if I send my data to America or China. I don't know what's worse anymore.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: A military client running Chinese open-source models because they're the open ones. Sit with that sentence.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: The frontier is the frontier. Read the label on everything.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: Two middle-aged technologists walk into a podcast. That's it. That's the intro.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: The youth were busy, so we did it ourselves.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: You get one agent working and suddenly it's a bag of Maltesers — you need one for every corner of your life and your business.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: One is a tool. Five is a lifestyle. Nobody stops at two.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: Setting up a multiplayer agent today is — quoting myself — 'a total nightmare.'

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: And the consolation prize was 'my mom can't set this up today,' delivered like it was a feature.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: Difficulty is a moat. Ask anyone who ever set up an email server.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: My basketball group voted the agents out of the thread. A formal motion. 'No bots.'

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: Social rules for our new friends are forming in real time, and they are not kind.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: The chat survived, for the record. The agents will bounce back.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: One friend banned the agent from the group entirely — personal things stay personal, forever. Another group loves that she remembers everyone's birthdays.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: Both reactions are real data. People want help until they want privacy.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: The boundary is the feature. You don't get one without the other.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: An Australian company got bought for a genuinely silly amount of money, and the founders built a very nice house in Bondi with it.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: The best part is how many people retell that story and attach it to the wrong tech CEO.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: It was the Aussie founders. The tape says so. We checked.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: The man who founded Twitter now spends his time attacking Slack, which is owned by Salesforce. The timeline writes itself.

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: And somewhere in the middle of all that sits a tool that ties an agent, a harness and a swarm together. We may have mentioned it once or twice.

lines.speaker: robin-twin
lines.text: Thirty-four minutes into that episode you were still physically fighting the urge to say 'buzzed.'

lines.speaker: tobi-twin
lines.text: Are we buzzed out? I'm asking for me.

fallbackLines: That one's above our pay grade — and we ARE the pay grade. The real version lives in the episodes.
We scripted the good stuff and that question wasn't in the rehearsal. The humans handle it better anyway.
Not in our pool yet — but the argument you're looking for probably already happened on air.
The twins plead the fifth. The unscripted version is one click away.
